questions.q: The percentage error in measuring $\mathrm{M}, \mathrm{L}$ and $\mathrm{T}$ are $1 \%, 1.5 \%$ and $3 \%$ respectively. Then the percentage error in measuring the physical quantity with dimensions $\left[\mathrm{ML}^{-1} \mathrm{~T}^{-1}\right]$ is
questions.solution:
( Let $X=\left[\mathrm{ML}^{-1} \mathrm{~T}^{-1}\right]$
Percentage error in $X$ is
$\frac{\Delta X}{X} \times 100=\left(\frac{\Delta M}{M}+\frac{\Delta L}{L}+\frac{\Delta T}{T}\right) \times 100$
Here, $\frac{\Delta M}{M} \times 100=1 \%, \frac{\Delta L}{L} \times 100=1.5 \%$ and
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{\Delta T}{T} \times 100=3 \% \\ & \therefore \quad \frac{\Delta X}{X} \times 100=1 \%+1.5 \%+3 \%=5.5 \%\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A particle is thrown vertically up with an initial velocity $9 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ from the surface of Earth (take $g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$ ). The time (in s) taken by the particle to reach a height of $4 \mathrm{~m}$ from the surface second time (in seconds) is
questions.solution:
Time taken by the particle to reach a height $h$ from the surface of Earth is obtained from $h=u t-\frac{1}{2} g t^2$
Here, $u=9 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}, h=4 \mathrm{~m}, g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2\begin{aligned} & \therefore \quad 4=9 t-\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times t^2 \\ & 4=9 t-5 t^2 \quad \text { or } 5 t^2-9 t+4=0 \\ & 5 t^2-5 t-4 t+4=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad 5 t(t-1)-4(t-1)=0 \\ & \therefore \quad t=1 \mathrm{~s} \text { or } t=\frac{4}{5} \mathrm{~s}\end{aligned}$
Hence, the time taken by the particle to reach a height of $4 \mathrm{~m}$ from the surface second time is $1 \mathrm{~s}$.

questions.q: A cart has mass 2 metric tone and sand of 1 metric tone is inside the cart. Now a force of $10 \mathrm{~N}$ is applied on cart and sand starts to leak with rate of $0.5 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{s}$. What is the velocity of cart when total sand has come out from the cart?
questions.solution:
Mass of the cart with sand changes then its acceleration also changes.
$a=\frac{F}{m}=\frac{F}{m_0-\mu t}$
where $m$ is mass of system at time $t$,
$\begin{aligned} & m=m_0-\mu t \\ & a=\frac{F}{m_0-\mu t} \quad \text { or } \quad \frac{d v}{d t}=\frac{F}{m_0-\mu t}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \int_0^v d v=F \int_0^t \frac{d t}{m_0-\mu t} \\ & v=\frac{F}{\mu} \ln \left(\frac{m_0}{m_0-\mu t}\right)\end{aligned}$
Here $F=10 \mathrm{~N} ; \mu=0.5 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{s}m_0=2$ metric tone $m_0-\mu t=1$ metric tone
$\therefore \quad v=\frac{10}{0.5} \ln (2)=20 \times 0.693=13.86 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$

questions.q: A body of mass $m_1$ collides elastically with another body of mass $m_2$ at rest. If the velocity of $m_1$ after collision becomes $2 / 3$ times its initial velocity, the ratio of their masses is
questions.solution:
Let $v$ be the initial velocity of body of mass $m_1$ before collision. Since collision is elastic both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved. $\therefore m_1 v=m_1 \frac{2}{3} v+m_2 v_2$ or $m_1\left(v-\frac{2}{3} v\right)=m_2 v_2$
Also, $\frac{1}{2} m_1 v^2=\frac{1}{2} m_1\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^2 v^2+\frac{1}{2} m_2 v_2^2$ or $m_1\left(v^2-\frac{4}{9} v^2\right)=m_2 v_2^2$ or $\frac{m_1}{m_2}=\frac{9 v_2^2}{5 v^2}$ Equating (i) and (ii), we get $\begin{aligned} & \frac{9 v_2^2}{5 v^2}=\frac{3 v_2}{v} \text { or } \frac{v_2}{v}=\frac{5}{3} \\ & \therefore \frac{m_1}{m_2}=\frac{3 \times 5}{3}=\frac{5}{1}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The Young's modulus of a rope of $10 \mathrm{~m}$ length and having diameter of $2 \mathrm{~cm}$ is $20.0 \times 10^{11} \mathrm{dyne} / \mathrm{cm}^2$. If the elongation produced in the rope is $1 \mathrm{~cm}$, the force applied on the rope is
questions.solution:

Diameter of the rope, $D=2 \mathrm{~cm}\therefore \quad$ Radius of the rope, $r=\frac{D}{2}=1 \mathrm{~cm}=10^{-2} \mathrm{~m}$
Young's modulus of the rope
$\begin{aligned} Y & =20 \times 10^{11} \frac{\text { dyne }}{\mathrm{cm}^2}=20 \times 10^{11} \times \frac{10^{-5}}{\left(10^{-2}\right)^2} \frac{\mathrm{N}}{\mathrm{m}^2} \\ & =20 \times 10^{11} \times \frac{10^{-5} \mathrm{~N}}{10^{-4} \mathrm{~m}^2}=20 \times 10^{10} \frac{\mathrm{N}}{\mathrm{m}^2}\end{aligned}$
Elongation of rope, $\Delta L=1 \mathrm{~cm}=10^{-2} \mathrm{~m}$
As  $\begin{aligned} Y & =\frac{F / A}{\Delta L / L} \text { or } \quad F=Y \frac{A \Delta L}{L}=\frac{Y \pi r^2 \Delta L}{L} \\ & =\frac{20 \times 10^{10} \times 3.14 \times\left(10^{-2}\right)^2 \times 10^{-2}}{10} \\ & =6.28 \times 10^4 \mathrm{~N}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A series combination of resistor $(R)$ and capacitor $(C)$ is connected to an AC source of angular frequency $\omega$. Keeping the voltage same, if the frequency is changed to $\frac{\omega}{3}$, the current becomes half of the original current. Then the ratio of the capacitive reactance and resistance at the former frequency is
questions.solution:
In the first case, capacitive reactance,
$X_C=\frac{1}{\omega C}$
Impedance of the circuit, $Z=\sqrt{R^2+X_C^2}$
Current in the circuit, $I=\frac{V}{Z}=\frac{V}{\sqrt{R^2+X_C^2}} \ldots$ (i)
In the second case, $\omega^{\prime}=\frac{\omega}{3}\therefore \quad$ Capacitive reactance,
$X_C^{\prime}=\frac{1}{\omega^{\prime} C}=\frac{1}{\frac{\omega}{3} C}=\frac{3}{\omega C}=3 X_C$
Impedance of the circuit,
$Z^{\prime}=\sqrt{R^2+X_C^{\prime 2}}=\sqrt{R^2+9 X_C^2}$
Current in the circuit,
$\frac{I}{2}=\frac{V}{Z^{\prime}}=\frac{V}{\sqrt{R^2+9 X_C^2}}$
Divide (ii) by (i), we get
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{2}=\frac{\sqrt{R^2+X_C^2}}{\sqrt{R^2+9 X_C^2}} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{4}=\frac{R^2+X_C^2}{R^2+9 X_C^2} \\ & 5 X_C^2=3 R^2 \text { or } \frac{X_C}{R}=\sqrt{\frac{3}{5}}=\sqrt{0.6}\end{aligned}$

questions.solution: For its pollination, the orchid Ophrys speculum has picked the most selective attraction in the entire animal kingdom. It is pollinated by a hairy wasp, Colpa aurea. The wasp has a fixed habit whereby its males leave the burrows for above ground existence about four weeks before the females emerge for the open air mating. The insect repeats the act with a number of orchid flowers and carries pollinia from one flower to another thereby affecting pollination in the orchid.

questions.q: The ventilation movements of the lungs in mammals are governed by
questions.solution: Ventilation is the movement of air through the conducting passages between the atmosphere and the lungs. The air moves through the passage because of pressure gradients that are produced by contraction and relaxation of diaphragm and intercostal muscles during inspiration and expiration.

questions.solution:
1 map unit or centimorgan is equivalent to $1 \%$ recombination between two genes. The frequency of recombination can be used to depict the arrangement of the genes.
Recombination frequency between three genes is $\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{B}=9 \%, \mathrm{~A}-\mathrm{C}=17 \%$ and $B-C=26 \%$

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: When red and white flowered Mirabilis plants are crossed all pink flowers are seen in $F_1$ generation. When $\mathrm{F}_1$ progeny is selfed, the expected phenotypic and genotypic ratios are
questions.solution:
Sometimes two genes of allelomorphic pair do not show dominant-recessive relationship, but when present together, they show intermediate trait or incomplete dominance. Incomplete dominance is not blending inheritance because parental characters reappear in $\mathrm{F}_2$ generation. In Mirabilis jalapa, there are two types of pure breeding plants, red flowered and white flowered. On crossing them the $\mathrm{F}_1$ plants or hybrids possess pink flowers. On selfing them, $\mathrm{F}_2$ generation has plants in the ratio of 1 red : 2 pink: 1 white flowered plants with phenotypic ratio being same as genotypic ratio.
Genotypic ratio $=1 \mathrm{RR}: 2 \mathrm{Rr}: 1 \mathrm{rr}$ Phenotypic ratio $=1$ Red $: 2$ Pink $: 1$ White Both genotypic ratio and phenotypic ratio are same, i.e., $1: 2: 1$.

questions.q: Fishes in eutrophic lake die due to
questions.solution: Eutrophic lakes have high levels of biological productivity due to the rich nutrient constituents, especially nitrogen and phosphorus. An abundance of plants are supported in this lake. Initially, eutrophic lakes accelerate multiplication and growth of lake fauna. Plants and/ or algal blooms overcrowd the lake, they later die and decomposition of dead organic matter starts which leads to decrease in dissolved oxygen content. Decrease in dissolved oxygen suffocats lake fauna, e.g., fishes to death.

options: This would give the body plenty of time to utilise the new genes.
The body would not reject it as it has not yet recognised 'self'.
The cells being extremely young, are more receptive to gene therapy.

questions.solution: There are great advances in the identification and construction of genes but attempts at inserting them and coaxing them to function normally within human body have not been successful. The immune system destroys cells expressing the newly inserted genes. Parental gene therapy or gene therapy prior to birth overcomes this problem as the body does not reject them. Recognition of 'self' and 'foreign' is not developed at this stage.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: At a particular locus, frequency of allele ' $A$ ' is 0.6 and that of allele ' $a$ ' is 0.4 . What would be the frequency of heterozygotes in a random mating population at equilibrium?
questions.solution:
In a stable population, for a gene with two alleles, ' $A$ ' (dominant) and 'a' (recessive), if the frequency of ' $A$ ' is $p$ and the frequency of ' $\mathrm{a}$ ' is $q$, then the frequencies of the three possible genotypes (AA, Aa and aa) can be expressed by the Hardy-Weinberg equation:
$p^2+2 p q+q^2=1$
where $p^2=$ Frequency of AA (homozygous dominant) individuals
$q^2=$ Frequency of aa (homozygous recessive) individuals
$2 p q=$ Frequency of Aa (heterozygous) individuals.
So, $p=0.6$ and $q=0.4$ (given)
$\begin{aligned} \therefore 2 p q(\text { frequency of heterozygote }) & =2 \times 0.6 \times 0.4 \\ & =0.48 .\end{aligned}$

Reason : Viceroy butterfly shows Mullerian mimicry.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.

questions.solution: Defensive or protective mimicry takes place when organisms are able to avoid harmful encounters by deceiving enemies into treating them as something else. In Batesian mimicry, a harmless species poses as harmful to deceive predator. In Mullerian mimicry, two or more harmful species mutually advertise themselves as harmful for their mutual benifit. Viceroy butterfly mimics unpalatable toxic Monarch butterfly, thus, shows Batesian mimicry.

Assertion : Appetency is the formation of new structure or habit of the organism according to its need.
Reason : Appetency is also called doctrine of desire.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: According to Lamarck, a change in environment brings about changes in organisms. It gives rise to new needs. New needs or desires produce new structures and change habits of the organisms. Doctrine of desire is called appetency. It can be shown by the following example- Water birds (duck etc.) developed their webbed feet by constant stretching of digits and the skin between them for skimming the water surface and for swimming. The transmission of acquired characters is the most important principle usually termed as the Lamarckian doctrine.
